title: The Stone Aqueduct
story:
Leaving the thatched shelter behind as the morning mist dissolved into soft rain, James continued his descent toward the valley floor. He walked along narrow stone ledges that held rows of tall green maize, their broad leaves dripping with fresh dew. He passed small stone storage huts built directly into the hillside. He passed wooden sluice gates that channeled mountain runoff from one terrace to the next. He passed bundles of dried corn husks bound neatly with twine, left by farmers who had already begun their day's work.

Below the agricultural terraces, where the steep slopes flattened into gentle meadows, stood the sweeping span of an ancient stone aqueduct. James reached the massive stone structure just as the sun broke through the clouds, casting golden light across the moss-covered masonry. Cool, clear spring water ran through an open trough along the top of the high wall, rushing downward toward distant farmhouses clustered across the valley floor.

James climbed up onto a flat stone buttress near the base of the aqueduct's central arch to rest his legs. He unclipped his brass map canister and laid it across his lap. Looking back toward the north, the towering wall of Cloudveil Ridge stood shrouded in gray clouds, completely hiding the path he had taken from Oakhaven. The cozy Archive Nook high under the library rafters felt a world away now—a quiet chapter tucked neatly behind him, never to be inhabited again.

Pulling his polished brass compass from around his neck, James watched the needle settle steadily toward the south. Beside him, water bubbled musically through the carved stone channels, reflecting the bright sky overhead. James dipped his paw into the trough, letting the freezing mountain runoff rinse away the dust of the trail, before looking out along the aqueduct's endless arc into the green valley beyond.
